# Telescoping Sum — Watch Interior Terms Cancel

## The identity to remember

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n}(f(k+1)-f(k))=f(n+1)-f(1)
$$

**Every symbol explained:** f is any function defined on the relevant integer indices; k runs from 1 to n; Σ adds n differences. All intermediate values appear once positive and once negative.

**Substitute actual numbers:** Take f(k)=k², n=3. The terms are (4−1)+(9−4)+(16−9)=3+5+7=15. The right side is 16−1=15.

## Why it is true

Expand the sum and write consecutive brackets. Every +f(j) cancels −f(j) from the next term for j=2..n, leaving only the final and initial values.

## When to recognise it

Use when seeing differences between consecutive states, amortised potential changes, or sums of rational expressions decomposed into differences.

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

Sum 1/(k(k+1)) by writing 1/k−1/(k+1). For k=1..3, the sum is 1−1/4=3/4.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

Cancellation requires the sequence of indexed terms to match exactly; careless changes of starting index lead to off-by-one errors.

## Your turn

Simplify Σ from k=1 to 5 of (1/k−1/(k+1)).

**Memory rule:** Reconstruct the cancellation or counting argument before memorising the formula.
